newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister sees end to southeast emergency rule.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister sees end to southeast emergency rule.

text.p: Turkish deputy prime minister Bulent Ecevit said on Tuesday emergency rule enforced in the mainly Kurdish southeast could be lifted within months if certain conditions were met, Anatolian news agency said.

"On the condition there is the necessary cooperation between the security forces...and the government departments, it will be possible to end emergency rule within the year," the state-run agency quoted Ecevit as saying.

Emergency rule, one step short of martial law, has been in force in nine southeastern provinces since 1987. The rule gives police and security forces wide powers of arrest and detention in their fight against Kurdish rebels in the area.

More than 26,000 people have been killed in the 13-year conflict between the Turkish armed forces and the rebels of the Kurdistan Workers Party who are fighting for independence or autonomy in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
